headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default data-leak and prompt-injection pathways between Flowise and gpt-engineer.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write files and run browser/tool nodes, while gpt-engineer reads/writes the project directory and uses stdin/stdout. If Flowise outputs attacker-controlled content into shared files, gpt-engineer may treat it as instructions. This is not provably blocked, though it needs a shared file bridge rather than a direct channel.
conditions: IF Flowise writes untrusted content into a project file that gpt-engineer later ingests
IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or copied artifacts
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files
Add a manual review step before gpt-engineer reads Flowise outputs
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and handles model provider keys and tool credentials; gpt-engineer touches generated source code and can execute code with the user's privileges. Both have broad network egress and filesystem access, so sensitive content can flow from Flowise into gpt-engineer outputs or external APIs in default deployments.
conditions: IF Flowise chatflow inputs include secrets or regulated data
IF gpt-engineer is allowed to read the same workspace or generated artifacts
IF either agent forwards those contents to configured model providers or tools
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspaces
Use separate API keys and principals per agent
Restrict network egress to approved endpoints
Redact sensitive fields before handoff
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and read the filesystem, and both support multiple instances with shared state via datastore or project directory. That creates overlapping write access and race conditions on shared artifacts, though the profiles do not show git-state conflicts or unrestricted shell overlap on the same repo by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or datastore concurrently
IF one agent overwrites files the other is reading or generating
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Snapshot outputs before handoff
Limit each agent to read-only access outside its own workspace
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder that can emit tool outputs, and gpt-engineer writes files then offers to run code with the user's privileges. If Flowise-produced content is treated as authoritative by gpt-engineer, a bad instruction or hallucinated fact can cascade into generated code or execution with real side effects.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer consumes Flowise output without verification
IF the resulting code is executed with user privileges
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Insert a validation step between agents
Constrain gpt-engineer to generate-only mode
Log and diff all handoffs
requires-engineering: add schema validation for Flowise outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, while gpt-engineer handles generated source code and can execute code with user privileges. The profiles show no explicit residency or certification mismatch, but they do show different data classes and retention-sensitive artifacts, so a compliance gap is plausible if regulated data is routed through both.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Flowise chatflows and then copied into gpt-engineer projects
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two workspaces
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared flows
Document retention for both workspaces
Use separate storage policies per agent
Purge temporary artifacts after each run
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both systems
